title: Building a mechanical trading EA in Tanzania for 3 years. Is anyone else doing this seriously?
author: confidentialpick
selftext:
Hi guys,

I’m reaching out to see if there are any other serious systematic/algo traders in Tanzania (or East Africa) who are actually building something real.

For the last 3 years, I’ve been teaching myself how to build and validate a mechanical trading EA. I don’t use discretionary price action, ICT, or gut feelings. It’s purely rules-based: specific ADX filters, ATR-based stop losses, and strict risk management (currently running a validated +0.39R expectancy on the V25 5-minute chart after 200+ forward-tested trades).

I’ve worked hard to get to a point where the system runs mechanically. I even partner with a developer abroad to keep the code sharp. But honestly, the hardest part is doing this alone.

Most people around me don’t understand systematic trading. They either think it’s a scam, or they’re trying to get rich quickly through sports betting or copying random signals. It’s hard to find someone to talk to who actually understands concepts like forward-testing vs. backtesting, expectancy, or the reality of dealing with local internet/VPS challenges.

I’m not selling anything. I’m not a guru. I’m just a builder looking for 1 or 2 genuine people who are also in the trenches of algo trading.

If you have a working system, understand the math behind trading, and are open to sharing knowledge or collaborating, let’s connect. Drop a comment or DM me.

(If you’re here to pitch a course or a "guaranteed profit" bot, please respect my time and skip this).

Thanks for reading.

comments.author: AlgoTradingQuant
comments.body: I assume you use a backtesting framework like backtesting.py for strategy verification?  I’ve been doing this for many years and every automated bot I built was custom made by me and running in the cloud.

replies.author: confidentialpick
replies.body:
Thanks for the direct question.To answer strictly,
The +0.39R expectancy is calculated over 208 forward-tested trades  live/demo execution, not backtested.
Zero curve-fitting. Parameters ADX threshold, ATR-based SL/TP, piprange/offset buffers,were set based on volatility mechanics, then locked. I didn't optimize the window; I validated it forward.
On the spread point: You're right. Deriv controls the spread, and it's the main friction. My EA includes a spread filter (pauses if >1.5x 20-period average) and the expectancy math already factors in real spread/slippage costs. If Deriv structurally shifts the spread regime, I monitor rolling 20-trade expectancy and pause/re-calibrate if it drops below +0.15R.
Happy to share my forward-test log structure or jump on a quick call if you're also working with synthetics or algorithmic execution. Respect the technical scrutiny.

replies.author: confidentialpick
replies.body: Appreciate the question. I actually don’t use Python or backtesting.py. I build with FXDreema (visual block logic) and export to native MQL5, running on a low-latency VPS. For verification, I skip heavy backtesting because Deriv’s historical tick data can be unreliable, so I rely entirely on forward testing—200+ live/demo trades with strict logging and rolling expectancy checks.

comments.body: V25 is the Deriv synthetic, so the price is their generator at a fixed volatility. an ADX filter can still find structure in it, but whatever edge you have is mostly against their spread, and that moves when they change it. how many trades is the +0.39R over, and how much of that window did you tune on?

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: 208 forward trades is a real sample, more than most posts here ever show. on V25 I'd log the spread at entry next to every trade, since it's Deriv's number to set and part of that R depends on it staying where it is.
